updates.title: Fixed: a saved contract disappearing
notes: A one-time cleanup, added when ClientFlow stopped shipping a contract of its own, was removing any template that matched that old example word for word — on every load, not just once.
Anyone who pasted in the sample wording lost their template each time they reopened the app. The cleanup is gone; your template is yours and stays put.
If yours vanished, paste it back in once under Settings → My contract. It will stick this time.

A gig's fee is no longer typed twice: once it has been invoiced, the gig adds its invoices up for you and the field becomes a figure rather than a box. Before that it asks for a quoted fee as a placeholder, which seeds the first invoice and the contract.

updates.title: Saved packages, and what a gig really leaves you
notes: Save the line items you use on most invoices — a sound package at its usual price with RCF 945 ×2, Wireless Microphone ×2 and the rest listed underneath — and drop one onto an invoice in a click instead of typing it again.
Already typed a line you'll reuse? Hit the 💾 next to it and it goes straight into your library.
Manage them in Settings → My packages, or from the picker itself. Editing a saved package never changes invoices already sent.
Gigs now take expenses: labour, the van, fuel, rentals, lodging, contractors. Add them on the gig and the form totals as you type, showing what's left of the fee.

The gig then shows what it brings in, what it costs and what you keep, broken down by category, with the margin worked out. Once a gig is invoiced the invoice total is used instead of the booking fee.
The dashboard gained a “Kept in” figure: what you collected this year less what the year's gigs cost you.
Fixed: for the first fraction of a second after any dialog opened, typing could land in the first field instead of the one you clicked.

Fixed: the save button crowded the COMP toggle on an invoice line, pushing the remove button onto a line of its own. Line items now lay out cleanly, and fold onto two rows on a phone instead of being squeezed.
A contract's fee now follows the money: pick a gig and it uses what that gig has been invoiced, pick an invoice and it uses that invoice's total. A fee you typed yourself is never overwritten.

updates.title: Google stops asking every hour
notes: Google permissions last exactly one hour and a browser app never gets a refresh token, so Gmail sending and the calendar kept popping a sign-in window. ClientFlow now renews that permission quietly in the background.
Your Google permission is also remembered per account and survives closing the tab — it used to live only as long as the tab did, so reopening the app meant signing in again.
The Calendar page no longer fires a sign-in window on load. Browsers block popups nobody clicked for, which looked like the calendar was broken; it now shows a Reconnect button instead.
Signing out, or switching to another account in the same browser, now clears the Google permission with it.
Quiet renewal needs the project's OAuth client id in firebase-config.js — see the README. Without it everything still works, Google just asks again each hour.

updates.title: Running order for multi-day bookings
notes: A wedding weekend is one booking with several functions, so a gig now takes a running order: each function with its own date, start and end time, and its own venue when it moves.
The calendar lists each day's functions under the booking, so Oct 17 reads Baraat, Wedding, Cocktail Hour, Reception instead of just the booking's name four times.
In your contract, {{eventSchedule}} writes the running order out with each date as its own sub-heading, and {{eventVenues}} lists each venue with the dates it covers.
Adding a function outside the dates you set widens the booking rather than letting it fall off the calendar.
A single-set gig is unchanged — leave the running order empty and the contract uses the gig's own date and time as before.

updates.title: Contracts you can send and sign
notes: New Contracts section. ClientFlow doesn't come with a contract of its own — the first time you open it, it asks for yours.
Paste in the agreement you already use (copied out of Word, Google Docs or a PDF) and it's split into editable sections, or start from a blank outline of the usual headings and write your own.
Swap the bits that change — the client, the date, the fee — for placeholders like {{clientName}} or {{fee}} and they fill themselves in on every contract after that.
Draw one up per gig and the client, venue, dates, fee, deposit, overtime rate and cancellation terms come across from records you already have.
Sign it yourself — type your name or draw it — then send the client a private link. They read it and sign from a phone or laptop, and their signature comes straight back here, timestamped.
The wording is frozen the moment a contract is created, so what gets signed can never drift from what was read. Editing your template later only affects new contracts.
Track everything at a glance: Draft → Out for signature → Signed, with tick marks for who has signed. Unsigned contracts also show up in Reminders.
Withdraw a link or void a contract any time — anyone still holding the link gets a short note instead.
Needs cloud sync, so it only shows up when you're signed in.

updates.title: Live quote links
notes: Share any quote or invoice on a private link — open it and hit "🔗 Share live link", then copy it, text it, or email it through Gmail or your mail app.
The page keeps itself current: change a price, add a package or log a deposit and what the client is looking at updates on its own, even if they already have it open. No re-sending.
They see the quote, what's been paid and what's still owed — never your other clients, their own contact details, or your internal gig notes.
"Stop sharing" switches a link off; anyone still holding it gets a short note instead of a broken page. Sharing again creates a brand-new link and the old one stays dead.
Deleting an invoice takes its live link down with it.
Needs cloud sync, so the link only shows up when you're signed in.
